office_does: Chelan PUD's five elected commissioners set policy, approve plans and budgets, and set rates for the county's public utility, which owns the Rock Island hydropower project now up for federal relicensing.
race_blurb: Open seat: Commissioner Garry Arseneault, who has held District 1 since 2015, is not on the ballot. Water and agricultural lawyer Colleen Frei and Malaga orchardist and EMT Aaron Young are running for the six-year term, and all of Chelan County votes in the general.

candidates.summary: Managing partner of JDSA Law, practicing agricultural and water law, and a consultant to growers' and winegrowers' associations, running for her first elected office on Rock Island relicensing, water stewardship and affordable rates.
highlights: Calls federal relicensing of the Rock Island project 'an incredibly important negotiation' for local power rights [S4]
Would advocate grid modernization that protects rates for local families and small businesses as tech demand grows [S4]
Pledges to protect local control and public ownership of the PUD [S1]
Endorsers listed on her site include Linda Evans Parlette and Frank Kuntz [S5]

candidates.summary: Malaga tree-fruit grower, general contractor and part-time EMT with 18 years as a volunteer firefighter, running on rate protection, data-center cost allocation and south-county representation.
highlights: Says he 'will stand firm against rate hikes that burden families, farms, and businesses' [S3]
Would ensure data centers and other large users don't shift costs onto residents and agriculture [S3]
Says he is the only candidate living south of downtown Wenatchee [S1]
Lists eight years on the Chelan County Republican Central Committee executive board and a seat on the county Boundary Review Board [S1]
